events.headline: Buccaneers add kicker Chase McLaughlin (right groin/hip) to the injury report on a Thursday-night week; no practice-squad kicker
events.detail: McLaughlin did not participate Tuesday with a right groin/hip injury ahead of Thursday night at Dallas. He is 9 of 9 on field goals with a long of 59 and 7 of 7 on extra points, and has scored 34 of Tampa Bay's 76 points. The Bucs carry no practice-squad kicker, so they would have to sign one if he cannot go. Baker Mayfield (right thumb) and Antoine Winfield Jr. (ribs) also did not practice.
events.so_what: A Thursday game leaves one more practice report before kickoff, so McLaughlin holders need a fallback kicker picked up before Thursday rather than Sunday. His value is built on long makes, which score the top distance bands here; a groin on the plant leg is exactly the injury that shortens range, so even if he plays, treat him as a weaker start than his 9-for-9 suggests.

events.headline: Lamar Jackson (ankle sprain) trending toward missing Week 5 at Atlanta, with one to two weeks the working timeline
events.detail: Update to the Oct. 5 item. NBC Sports' Week 5 injury report (Oct. 6) puts Jackson's chance to play Sunday night at the Falcons as an "outside chance" and says he is likely out one to two weeks. Ian Rapoport reported Monday the injury is an ankle sprain that is not considered long-term, and Jesse Minter said he does not think it is "going to be crazy long-term." He left the stadium in a walking boot after a sack at the end of the first half against Tennessee. Tyler Huntley would start; he went 8 of 9 for 63 yards in relief.
events.so_what: Plan for Jackson to sit this week and possibly next. A Sunday-night kickoff makes any late reversal the worst kind of game-time call, so anyone starting him without a second QB should already have a Sunday-afternoon streamer rostered. Huntley is a deep streamer only and removes most of the konami rushing premium. Zay Flowers keeps his volume either way, with less touchdown upside from Huntley.

source.label: NBC Sports Week 5 injury report, Oct. 6

events.headline: Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) likely out Week 5 vs. Dolphins; Tee Higgins (adductor) closer to doubtful, with a Week 6 bye behind it
events.detail: Update to the Oct. 5 item. NBC Sports' Oct. 6 injury report lists Chase as likely out for Week 5 while he remains in the concussion protocol, and Higgins (adductor) as day-to-day but probably closer to doubtful. Zac Taylor said Monday both are day-to-day. Cincinnati has its bye in Week 6, so sitting either player against 0-4 Miami buys him two full weeks. Taylor named practice-squad receivers Noah Thomas and Jordan Moore as candidates for more work.
events.so_what: Line up Week 5 without both Bengals receivers and treat any upgrade as a bonus; the bye right behind this game removes the team's reason to rush either one. Chase Brown is the Bengals piece whose role grows. Chase and Higgins holders lose them for two straight weeks counting the bye, so the bench-depth crunch is real with only 5 bench spots.

source.label: NBC Sports Week 5 injury report, Oct. 6

events.headline: Baker Mayfield (thumb) misses Monday and Tuesday practice; Jalon Daniels makes his second start Thursday at Dallas
events.detail: Mayfield, who dislocated his right (throwing) thumb in Week 3, did not practice Monday or Tuesday, and the Buccaneers expect undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels to start Thursday night against the Cowboys. Todd Bowles confirmed Daniels "will be the quarterback Thursday night." Bowles had put Mayfield's absence at about three weeks; there was no ligament or tendon damage. CeeDee Lamb (thigh) was a full participant for Dallas on Tuesday.
events.so_what: Mayfield is not a Week 5 option, and with Week 6 the earliest realistic return he stays a bench hold for anyone with a second QB. Daniels is not a streaming answer on a short week on the road. Tampa Bay's pass catchers drop a notch with a rookie throwing, which matters most for the touchdown side of their scoring.

events.headline: Ladd McConkey aggravates his foot at Seattle, called "week-to-week" by Jim Harbaugh
events.detail: Update to the Oct. 4 item. McConkey was active against the Seahawks but aggravated the same foot injury that had him questionable, played 24 snaps, failed to catch either of his two targets and was ruled out in the third quarter. Harbaugh called him "week-to-week" on Monday, while ESPN's Kris Rhim reported he may be closer to day-to-day. The first Chargers injury report comes Wednesday. Quentin Johnston and Tre' Harris are Justin Herbert's top two wideouts if McConkey sits.
events.so_what: Not a fact you can set a lineup on yet: if he is healthy enough to practice Wednesday he is a FLEX, otherwise plan around him. Johnston is the main beneficiary of any absence; Harris is a speculative add only. The Chargers line is also falling apart (Joe Alt and Trevor Penning both hurt), which caps every Chargers pass catcher.

events.headline: Seahawks pass on Joe Mixon after his physical, sign Robert Henry Jr. instead
events.detail: Seattle decided not to sign Mixon to its practice squad after a physical, per ESPN's Adam Schefter, and will add Robert Henry Jr. from Washington's practice squad. Mixon, 30, missed all of 2025 with a foot injury and was released by Houston in March. Emanuel Wilson had 21 carries for 81 yards and a TD plus three catches for 39 yards and a score against the Chargers; Jadarian Price is on IR and Zach Charbonnet has opened his practice window.
events.so_what: Wilson's lead role survives at least until Charbonnet returns, so he stays a volume FLEX. Mixon is not a stash anywhere until a team actually signs him.

events.headline: Texans will open Tank Dell's 21-day practice window this week, DeMeco Ryans says
events.detail: Ryans said Monday the 0-4 Texans expect to open the window for Dell, who has not played since the severe knee injury he suffered in Week 16 of 2024. Houston then has 21 days from his first practice to activate him or he reverts to season-ending IR. NBC Sports describes his return as likely a week-to-week proposition.
events.so_what: A practice is a step, not a clearance. Dell is a bench stash for a team with a spare spot, and nothing to start until he is activated and shows a role in a receiver room that has not produced a consistent secondary option.

events.headline: Bijan Robinson (145 yards, 2 TDs) and Brian Robinson (3 TDs) combine for five scores as Falcons rout Saints 45-24
events.detail: On Monday Night Football Bijan Robinson ran 19 times for 145 yards and two touchdowns, including a 59-yard run. Brian Robinson ran 14 times for 62 yards and scored all three of his touchdowns from inside the 12 (4, 8 and 11 yards). Michael Penix Jr. went 15 of 20 for 233 yards and a touchdown in a game Atlanta controlled throughout. Falcons left tackle Jake Matthews left 11 snaps in.
events.so_what: Bijan stays a locked RB1; the new information is that Brian Robinson owns the short-yardage carries in a blowout script, which makes him a TD-dependent FLEX option in weeks Atlanta is favored rather than a pure handcuff. Do not chase three scores on 62 yards as a stable floor. Watch Matthews' status for the run game.

events.headline: Chris Olave (knee) hurt on Saints' final drive after 8-116 night; Kellen Moore says he is "OK"; Alvin Kamara scores twice as lead back
events.detail: Olave caught 8 of 12 targets for 116 yards Monday, then took a hard hit to the knee on a five-yard catch with about 90 seconds left in the 45-24 loss and did not return. Moore said postgame that Olave was "OK," and Ari Meirov reported it was nothing serious, with Olave appearing fine at postgame handshakes. Alvin Kamara, leading the backfield with Travis Etienne on injured reserve (hamstring, earliest return Nov. 8), ran 7 times for 23 yards and two touchdowns and added 35 receiving yards; he briefly left with a knee issue in the third quarter and returned. Tyler Shough threw 48 times for 286 yards.
events.so_what: Olave is a forecast, not a clearance: start him, but check Wednesday's practice report before locking him in. Kamara's two goal-line scores on 23 rushing yards show the value is the TD and passing-game role, not efficiency, in a Saints offense that is chasing points. Etienne holders keep him stashed on IR.

events.headline: Tyreek Hill expected to sign "over the next few days," agent says; Chiefs among teams in talks
events.detail: Drew Rosenhaus told ESPN's Adam Schefter on Monday he anticipates Hill signing with a team within days. Kansas City reached out Sunday night after losing Tyquan Thornton (dislocated ankle, 12 to 16 weeks) and Rashee Rice (hamstring, possibly several weeks). Hill is recovering from the dislocated knee and torn ACL he suffered in Week 4 of 2025, and the Chiefs believe he is targeting a November return.
events.so_what: Nothing to start before November. If he lands in Kansas City he walks into a depleted receiver room with Mahomes, which makes him a bench stash worth a spot for anyone with room; anywhere else, wait for a practice before spending one. Rice holders should note a Hill signing would cap Rice's target share once both are healthy.

events.headline: Rashee Rice (hamstring) could miss several weeks; Tyquan Thornton out 12 to 16 weeks after ankle dislocation
events.detail: Rice pulled up on a first-quarter catch-and-run against the Raiders and did not return. Andy Reid called it a tweak, but The Athletic's Mike Silver reported Rice could be out several weeks. Kansas City has its bye in Week 5, so the first game he can miss is Week 6 against the Chargers. Thornton dislocated his ankle in the fourth quarter and needs surgery, with a possible late-season return.
events.so_what: Hold Rice through the bye and read the Week 6 practice reports; this is a bench stash, not a drop. With Thornton gone for months, the Chiefs' remaining receivers and tight ends absorb Mahomes' targets, so watch which one runs the most routes in Week 6.

events.headline: Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) unlikely before Week 7, with Week 9 the likelier debut
events.detail: Adam Schefter reported the Saints rookie, on IR since a training-camp hamstring injury and eligible to return Tuesday, is weeks away. Week 7 is the best case and Week 9 against Cleveland on Nov. 8 is the likelier target.
events.so_what: A stash only for a team with an open IR slot. He gives no help before November and then has to earn targets in an offense he has not played in yet.

events.headline: Saquon Barkley (hamstring) reported week-to-week and likely out for London vs. Jaguars; Tank Bigsby to IR, Will Shipley next up
events.detail: Update to the Oct. 4 item. Monday reporting moved Barkley to week-to-week with the hamstring, and he is considered likely to miss the Week 5 game against the Jaguars in London; Ian Rapoport said it does not initially seem "overly serious" and Nick Sirianni deferred a formal update to Wednesday's first practice. Bigsby, who replaced Barkley on Sunday, will have core-muscle surgery and go on injured reserve, missing at least four games. Will Shipley, who ran six times for 23 yards Sunday, is the only healthy back on the depth chart.
events.so_what: Plan on no Barkley in Week 5 and set the lineup around it rather than waiting on Wednesday. Bigsby is a drop or an IR stash, not the pickup; Shipley is the Eagles back to claim, but Philadelphia will likely add a veteran, so treat him as a one- or two-week volume play. Hold Barkley.

events.headline: Kyle Monangai (thumb) "day-to-day," Ben Johnson says, after 30-carry, two-TD game vs. Jets
events.detail: Update to the Oct. 4 item. Johnson said Monday the right thumb injury is not serious: "We think he is going to be ok... more of a day-to-day type deal." Monangai ran 30 times for 146 yards and two TDs Sunday after D'Andre Swift lost a third-quarter fumble and sat the final three drives; Swift finished with 15 carries for 58 yards. Chicago hosts Green Bay in Week 5 with Tyson Bagent at QB.
events.so_what: The thumb looks minor, so Monangai stays the add of the week and a FLEX start in a split with Swift. A fumble benching is not a demotion yet; expect Swift back in the rotation, which caps both backs until one wins the early-down work for a second week.

events.headline: D.J. Moore (shoulder) not a long-term issue but could miss Week 5 vs. Rams
events.detail: Update to the Oct. 4 item. Adam Schefter reported the re-aggravated shoulder is not a long-term problem, but Moore might miss Week 5 against the Rams. Buffalo has its bye in Week 7. Moore hurt the same shoulder in Week 2 and had been limited in practice since without missing a game.
events.so_what: Plan for a missed game: keep a healthy FLEX ready and check Wednesday's report. Do not drop him; this is a one- or two-week absence with a bye shortly after.

events.headline: Zach Charbonnet (knee) won't play Week 5 vs. 49ers; Emanuel Wilson keeps the lead role
events.detail: Update to the Oct. 3 item. Mike Macdonald said Monday that Charbonnet will take team reps in practice this week but will not play against San Francisco, which points to Week 6 at the earliest. Jadarian Price is on IR until Week 8. Wilson handled 75% of the backfield carries in Sunday's win over the Chargers, with 81 rushing yards, three catches for 39 yards and two total TDs.
events.so_what: Wilson is a FLEX start again in Week 5 on volume and goal-line work. Charbonnet is a stash that turns into a committee around Week 6.

events.headline: Ben Johnson names Tyson Bagent the Bears starter for Week 5 vs. Packers with Caleb Williams (hamstring) out
events.detail: Update to the Oct. 3 item. After Bagent went 25 of 34 for 268 yards and an interception in the 23-12 win over the Jets, Johnson said Monday: "Tyson will be the guy, and we'll go forward from there." Williams remains out with a Grade 2 hamstring strain.
events.so_what: Keep Williams benched. Bagent moved the ball well enough that the Bears skill players are startable on their roles, but he is not a fantasy QB start. This is the Monangai and Swift backfield's game to carry.

events.headline: Marcus Mariota sprains his MCL in London; Jayden Daniels (elbow) must clear a full practice week for the Giants
events.detail: Update to the Oct. 2 item. Mariota left the loss to the Colts in the first quarter with his second MCL sprain of the year and is expected to miss time. Seventh-round rookie Athan Kaliakmanis played the rest of the game and threw his first NFL touchdown. Dan Quinn said Daniels would go through a full practice week on the team's return, which now decides whether Kaliakmanis starts Week 5 against the Giants. WR Jaylin Lane suffered an ankle fracture and dislocation and is likely out for the season.
events.so_what: Do not start Daniels until he gets through the week; if he is cleared, his rushing upside makes him a full-go QB1 again. If Kaliakmanis starts, every Washington pass catcher is a downgrade. Mariota is droppable.

events.headline: Ollie Gordon runs for 100 yards and a TD as the Dolphins' lead back vs. Vikings
events.detail: Update to the Oct. 1 item. With Jaylen Wright back from his stinger and Jeff Hafley having described a split, Gordon still led the Miami backfield in Week 4: 100 rushing yards and a touchdown on 22 snaps, about 56% of the backfield share.
events.so_what: Gordon has the early-down and goal-line role behind the departed De'Von Achane and is a FLEX start on that. A 56% share is still a committee, so Wright keeps some standalone value and Gordon is not a locked RB2 yet.

events.headline: Harbaugh says OC Mike McDaniel's job is "not in jeopardy" as 0-4 Chargers split RB work three ways
events.detail: After the loss at Seattle, Harbaugh said McDaniel "is a skilled coach, and we're going to keep growing." Omarion Hampton had just nine carries on 22 snaps and has fallen from ninth in the league in carries through Week 2 to 26th over the last two weeks, with Keaton Mitchell and Kimani Vidal taking more of the work; Harbaugh called the three-back rotation what is best for the team. Justin Herbert was pressured on 55% of dropbacks behind a line that also lost Joe Alt and Trevor Penning.
events.so_what: No scheme reset is coming, so assume the committee holds. Hampton slides from locked RB2 to a FLEX whose floor depends on goal-line work; Mitchell is the McDaniel speed back worth a bench spot, Vidal is not. A collapsing line lowers the ceiling for the whole offense.

events.headline: Kenyon Sadiq (back) active vs. Bears; Mason Taylor inactive
events.detail: Update to the Oct. 2 item. Sadiq, Questionable with a back injury, is not on the Jets' official inactive list. Inactive: RB Breece Hall, WR Adonai Mitchell, TE Mason Taylor, OG Dylan Parham, LB Kiko Mauigoa, CB Nahshon Wright and EDGE Kingsley Enagbare. Sadiq played 57.6% of snaps with a 7-105-1 line in Week 3 with Taylor out.
events.so_what: Start Sadiq as the streaming TE: active, with Taylor and Mitchell both out, he has the tight-end role to himself and an open share of the targets. Locks at the 1:00 ET kickoff.

source.label: The Jet Press, Jets Week 4 inactives, Oct. 4

events.headline: Tyjae Spears (ankle) active vs. Ravens; Tony Pollard cleared, Michael Carter inactive
events.detail: Update to the Oct. 2 item. Spears, Questionable after Robert Saleh said he had hurdles to clear, is not on the Titans' official inactive list. Inactive: RB Michael Carter, CB Jaylon Jones, OG Drew Moss, OT Brandon Crenshaw-Dickson, TE Kylen Granson and DT Jackie Marshall. Pollard had no designation and had 21 touches for 96 yards in Week 3.
events.so_what: Pollard stays a volume FLEX, but Spears being active takes back some of the passing-down work, so trim expectations a little. Spears himself is not a start in a split against Baltimore.

source.label: Yahoo Sports, Titans vs. Ravens inactives, Oct. 4

events.headline: DeVonta Smith inactive vs. Rams and unlikely for Week 5; Goedert, Brown, Lane Johnson also out
events.detail: Update to the Oct. 2 item. Smith (hamstring), Hollywood Brown, Dallas Goedert, LB Zack Baun and OTs Lane Johnson and Fred Johnson are on the Eagles' official inactive list. NFL Network's Mike Garafolo reports Smith is unlikely to return in Week 5 against Jacksonville. Dontayvion Wicks and rookie Makai Lemon take the receiver snaps, and Zach Ertz the extra tight-end work.
events.so_what: Bench all three, and plan on Smith missing Week 5 too. Wicks is the WR who absorbs volume and a deep FLEX this week; with two starting tackles out, temper expectations for the whole Eagles passing game. Wicks is the Tuesday FAAB target over Lemon.

events.headline: Terry McLaurin (hamstring) inactive for London vs. Colts; Daniels and White also out
events.detail: Update to the Oct. 3 item. McLaurin is on Washington's official inactive list along with Jayden Daniels (elbow), Rachaad White (shoulder) and WR Luke McCaffrey. Marcus Mariota starts. For Indianapolis, Keenan Allen (groin), WR Darius Slayton and RB DJ Giddens are inactive, with Josh Downs the top remaining Colts wideout. The game kicked off at 9:30 a.m. ET, so these lineups are already locked.
events.so_what: Nothing left to act on for this game. If McLaurin is still in a lineup it scores zero; there is no swap once London kicks off. Diggs was the right pivot as the first read for Mariota, and Antonio Williams a deep-league dart only.

source.label: Yahoo Sports, Colts vs. Commanders Week 4 inactives, Oct. 4

events.headline: Justin Jefferson (ankle) out vs. Dolphins, "hopeful" to return Week 5 at New Orleans
events.detail: Update to the Oct. 2 item. Jefferson is out for Week 4 after not practicing all week. ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported Saturday that he is hopeful to play in Week 5 against the Saints and the team does not view the ankle as a long-term problem. Kevin O'Connell has said Jefferson comes back only when he can "be himself."
events.so_what: Bench him this week and hold. "Hopeful" for Week 5 is a forecast, not a clearance; check Wednesday's practice report before planning around him. Jordan Addison gets the target bump for one week.
